# FDG8034

> DO implement `IEnumerable<T>` when designing new collections. Consider implementing `ICollection<T>`, `IReadOnlyList<T>`, or even `IList<T>` where it makes sense.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3.4 Implementing Custom Collections.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1010
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

CA1010 reports an externally visible type that implements IEnumerable, ICollection or IList, directly or through a base class such as CollectionBase, without the generic counterpart (probe with SDK 10.0.402). The second sentence (consider ICollection<T>, IReadOnlyList<T> or IList<T>) and the advice to follow the API pattern of Collection<T> are not checked, so coverage is partial. Adding the generic interface adds to the public API without changing a signature; CA1010 has no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
public class TextDecorationCollection : IList<TextDecoration> ... {
   ...
}
```

When implementing such a custom collection, follow the API pattern established by `Collection<T>` and `ReadOnlyCollection<T>` as closely as possible. That is, implement the same members explicitly, name the parameters in the same way that these two collections name them, and so on. In other words, make your custom collection different from these two collections only when you have a very good reason to do so.
